subject.title: [Feature]: Add Ralph Loop feature and add max iteration number into the agent configuration

question: Should OpenClaw support a first-class STOP-driven repeated-prompt orchestration mode, and if so should it live in core configuration or behind a generic plugin/runtime seam?
rationale: Source inspection establishes that this would add a new orchestration mode and public config contract, but repository policy and code cannot decide the intended ownership, safety semantics, or relationship to the separate hard iteration-budget proposal.

options.title: Define a generic seam first
options.body: Specify a reusable loop-controller contract with interruption, resume, budget, and STOP semantics, then implement Ralph behavior outside core unless a missing core primitive is proven.

options.title: Add a core Ralph mode
options.body: Introduce explicit global and per-agent configuration plus runtime wiring, accepting the additional core API and long-running session-state responsibility.

options.title: Decline native orchestration
options.body: Keep core limited to safety budgets and direct users to external orchestrators or plugins for repeated-prompt workflows.

recommendation.title: Define a generic seam first
recommendation.body: Specify a reusable loop-controller contract with interruption, resume, budget, and STOP semantics, then implement Ralph behavior outside core unless a missing core primitive is proven.

likelyOwner.reason: They already reviewed this exact product boundary and have relevant recent agent/config history.
